# Source access and requests

**Checked 22 October 2026.** “Available” means retrievable; “read” identifies the portions actually inspected. Accessible full text is not the same as an exhaustive review.

## Six full texts requested from the user

1. **Ariel Porat and Alex Stein (1997), “Liability for Uncertainty: Making Evidential Damage Actionable,” Cardozo Law Review 18:1891–1960.** [Record](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=10261). Needed for C004/C085. Abstract and publication metadata checked; full article unavailable. The earlier repository PDF route failed, and SSRN returned 403 during this pass.

2. **David Plunkett and Tim Sundell (2013), “Disagreement and the Semantics of Normative and Evaluative Terms,” Philosophers' Imprint 13(23):1–37.** [Publisher](https://quod.lib.umich.edu/p/phimp/3521354.0013.023/). Needed for C063. Institutional abstract accessible; ANU bitstream timed out, the author-linked copy failed, and Michigan returned 403.

3. **Deborah A. DeMott (2014), “The Fiduciary Character of Agency and the Interpretation of Instructions,” in Philosophical Foundations of Fiduciary Law.** [Duke record](https://scholarship.law.duke.edu/faculty_scholarship/3129/). Needed for C013. Repository description accessible; linked Duke PDF returned 403.

4. **Philip Pettit (2000), “Democracy, Electoral and Contestatory,” in Designing Democratic Institutions: NOMOS XLII, pp. 105–144.** [Author record](https://ppettit.scholar.princeton.edu/publications/democracy-electoral-and-contestatory). Needed for C013/C021. Publication verified; PhilPapers PDF returned 403 and the author-linked document failed.

5. **Emre Bayamlıoğlu (2018), “Contesting Automated Decisions: A View of Transparency Implications,” European Data Protection Law Review 4(4):433–446.** [DOI](https://doi.org/10.21552/edpl/2018/4/6). Needed for C021. Institutional abstract accessible; linked document and SSRN route failed.

6. **André Santos Campos (2026), “Decoupling Generational Sovereignty: The Cross-Temporal Role of the Sovereign People,” Moral Philosophy and Politics, online first, pp. 1–29.** [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1515/mopp-2025-0072). Needed for C111. Institutional abstract and metadata accessible; institutional PDF and publisher route failed.

If convenient, the **published opening chapter of Stephen Darwall's The Second-Person Standpoint (2006)** would help verify the version consulted for C045. A publicly posted draft was obtained; the final chapter and entire book were not reviewed. This is a version request, not a claim that no relevant Darwall text was accessible.

## Successfully obtained: actual reading boundaries

- **Cohen and Suzor (2024), “Contesting the public interest in AI governance.”** Full HTML available; introduction, §3.3 on independent information, conclusion, and surrounding context read. [Text](https://policyreview.info/articles/analysis/contesting-public-interest-ai-governance).
- **Beckers and Halpern (2019), “Abstracting Causal Models.”** Author PDF available; introduction, relevant exact/uniform/τ/strong/constructive abstraction definitions, and selected examples read. Proofs not independently verified. [PDF](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/home/halpern/papers/abstraction.pdf).
- **Belardinelli and Lomuscio (2017), “Agent-based Abstractions for Verifying Alternating-time Temporal Logic with Imperfect Information.”** Author PDF succeeded after proceedings endpoint failed. Introduction, definitions 1–4, and description of simulation/abstraction results read; proofs not independently checked. [PDF](https://www.doc.ic.ac.uk/~fbelard/Documents/aamas2017c.pdf).
- **Jamroga and Kim (2023), “Practical Abstraction for Model Checking of Multi-Agent Systems.”** Introduction and related-work map read to locate closer technical work. [PDF](https://proceedings.kr.org/2023/38/kr2023-0038-jamroga-et-al.pdf).
- **Flores and Woodard (2023), “Epistemic norms on evidence-gathering.”** Full HTML available; introduction and opening arguments in §2 read. [Text](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11098-023-01978-8).
- **Longino (2004), “How Values Can Be Good for Science.”** A first teaching scan lacked usable extracted text; a second university PDF succeeded. Introduction and pp. 133–135 read. [PDF](https://www.ugr.es/~zink/mono/Longino2004.pdf). No upload needed.
- **Friedman (2019), “Inquiry and Belief.”** Author accepted manuscript dated 2017 available; introduction, §2 opening, §4.1, and conclusion read. Cite the published 2019 article. [PDF](https://jfriedmanphilo.github.io/IB.pdf).
- **Liao and Sandberg (2008), “The Normativity of Memory Modification.”** Author manuscript available after FHI route failed; sections VII–VIII and IX opening read, including the entire moral-obligations section. - **Darwall (2006), The Second-Person Standpoint, opening-chapter draft.** Opening development of demands, authority, reasons, and accountability read. Not the entire book or verified final chapter. [Draft](https://www.princeton.edu/~msmith/mycourses/darwall-ch1-2006.pdf). No draft passages quoted or redistributed.
- **Beckman (2025), “Democratic Legitimacy and Decisions for the Future.”** Full HTML available; main argument, objections, and conclusion read. [Text](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11158-025-09717-y).
- **Hohnerlein (2024), “Democratic Revisability and the Legitimacy of Constitutional Entrenchments: A Content-Specific Approach.”** Publisher PDF available after HTML timeout; introduction and §B.III discussion of interpretation and democratic revision read. [Publication](https://doi.org/10.1017/glj.2024.27).
- **Angermeyer (2023), “Translation as discrimination: Sociolinguistics and inequality in multilingual institutional contexts.”** Full HTML available; introduction and institutional interpreting/participant-role discussions read. [Text](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/language-in-society/article/3F3FA2A20A605233DFE528A8C3C56A67).
- **Sadler, Baker, and Engebretsen (2024), “Translation and the Political: Antagonism and Hegemony.”** Accepted manuscript available; introduction and theoretical setup read. [Publication](https://doi.org/10.1080/14781700.2023.2186944).
- **Vredenburgh (2022), “The Right to Explanation.”** Author manuscript obtained after publisher failure; introduction, §4.1, and relevant cost discussion read. [PDF](https://researchonline.lse.ac.uk/id/eprint/121185/1/_The_Right_to_Explanation.pdf). No upload needed.
- **Karlan and Kugelberg (2025), “No right to an explanation.”** Full HTML available; introduction and §5 on normative reasons read. [Text](https://doi.org/10.1111/phpr.70008). No upload needed.

## Limits

Search leads were not treated as read sources. The entire Halpern book Actual Causality and the entire Darwall book were not reviewed. Legal spoliation doctrine, donor-intent law, interpreting ethics, and affirmative duties to substantiate demands need further comparison. No current legal or clinical claims are advanced; the essays use stipulated cases.

No search established the absence of a prior positive-assistance duty for C045, correction-cost principle for C004/C085, or procedural correction/referral duty for C063/C021. These remain material originality risks even after the requested PDFs arrive.
